Thanks again for walking through the sealed bundle flow earlier. We have the final signed bundle ready for physical transfer to our sterilized depot. Attached: acme-sealed-bundle-v3.tar.gz.sig and bundle-manifest-v3.json.

Key asks from our side before the courier picks up tomorrow:

- Confirm how Redwood wants to handle the KMS handover: we currently have a sealed envelope with the wrapped KEK; do you want the HSM slot assignment documented in the manifest or is that handled during operator ceremony?
- Proposed activation window: Thu Sep 9, 02:00–04:00 UTC (quiet hours for our tenants). Can Redwood accommodate that for a canary first, then broad activation by 08:00 UTC?

We also need a short rollback statement that our operators can rely on if the canary fails. Please cc the courier ops contact (ops@securecourier.com) so they can finalize ETA.

Thanks,
Bryan

Bryan — thanks for the packet. Quick answers and next steps below.

Operator acceptance checklist (we will share a one-page printout for the depot operator):
- Verify courier attestation (ID + sealed tamper-evidence)
- Confirm manifest hash matches acme-sealed-bundle-v3.tar.gz.sig (offline sha256sum)
- Validate image signature using Redwood root key (we'll supply root pubkey in manifest)
- Cold-boot test in a segregated rack (smoke-start container) — 10 minutes max
- KV-store / DB migration disabled for canary; full activation requires DB upgrade window approval

KMS / HSM handover:
- Procedure: Acme provides wrapped KEK inside sealed envelope. On operator acceptance, the operator will place the envelope into the HSM console and call the Redwood secure-ops phone line for a two-person unseal ceremony.
- HSM slot assignment: document the slot ID in the manifest AFTER unseal. We do not require the courier to observe slot assignment.

Activation schedule: Redwood can run a canary during Thu Sep 9, 02:30–03:00 UTC and hold for telemetry for 75 minutes. If metrics are green, we will proceed with staged rollouts to remaining racks, completing by 08:00 UTC.

Rollback statement (one-liner for operators):
- If canary health < 95% baseline for > 10 minutes OR manifest mismatch, power off affected canary rack, reimage from last approved snapshot, and contact Redwood on-call to initiate a signed rollback manifest.

I will attach a canary checklist and a short on-call escalation tree. Jordan — can you confirm the telemetry gating thresholds and how we will surface failures to Acme? David — please prep the signed rollback manifest template.

Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0199

On Thu, Sep 9, 2026 at 00:30 UTC Courier Ops <ops@securecourier.com> wrote:
> Pickup confirmed for Wed Sep 8 18:00 local (Acme HQ). ETA at sealed depot: Thu Sep 9 00:30 UTC.

Thanks all — couple operational clarifications and the canary checklist attached. Key points: 
- Telemetry gating: CPU load, memory footprint, error rate (5xx count), token latency p99. Canary must be stable for 45 minutes with error rate <0.5% and p99 latency within 1.3x baseline.
- Automatic fallback: continuous routing will divert traffic from canary racks to warm standby pool if any gate trips. Warm standby currently uses quantized model variant v3-q8.
- Signed rollback manifest: David — I need the rollback manifest filled with previous bundle hash and operator acknowledgement fields. Template attached as canary-activation-checklist.pdf and rollback-manifest-template.txt (we will hand these as paper copies to operators).

Escalation: if canary trips, operator will follow these steps in order — (1) stop traffic, (2) capture logs to sealed USB (hash), (3) reimage from snapshot, (4) call Redwood on-call. We will provide the one-line script to compute the offline sha256.

Jordan Blake
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference
